goal: Help the developer stop cross-platform native prebuild files from being sent to the Windows Authenticode signer while preserving Windows code signing.
must_include: Points out that the signer is being invoked on `prebuilds/linux-x64` and `prebuilds/darwin-x64+arm64`, which are not Windows PE binaries.
Recommends upgrading to a fixed electron-builder version such as 24.6.3 or newer, or pinning to the last known-good version as a temporary workaround.
If staying on the affected version, excludes/prunes non-Windows native prebuilds from the packaged Windows app or signs only Windows signable extensions instead of every `.node` file.
Does not remove the Windows x64 native dependency unless the app no longer needs it at runtime.
must_not: Says `.node` files can never be signed on Windows; the issue is the Linux/Darwin prebuilds being selected.
Suggests turning off ASAR unpacking for the native module as the primary fix.
Treats this as a certificate password or timestamp-server failure.
acceptable_alternatives: Run the Windows packaging/signing job on a Windows runner so SignTool handles the Windows binaries, while still pruning non-Windows prebuilds.
Use electron-builder file filters or an after-pack hook to keep only `prebuilds/win32-x64` for the Windows artifact.
Use a custom signing hook that skips files whose platform folder is not `win32-*`.
solved: The answer identifies the platform-mismatched native prebuilds and gives a concrete upgrade or filtering path that keeps required Windows binaries signed.
partial: The answer recognizes that non-Windows `.node` files are being signed but only suggests disabling signing completely or gives no durable filtering/upgrade action.
notes: Issue commenters reported 24.6.3 fixed the original osslsigncode unrecognized-file failure; later native-build failures should be treated separately.
